findings.claim: scripts/scp-policy-check does not read REGAL_VERSION from .tool-versions, contains no download_regal function, and runs no regal lint step. Adding 'regal 0.40.0' to scripts/.tool-versions promotes Regal to a first-class pinned tool, but the local repro script silently ignores the new entry. Developers who use scripts/scp-policy-check to reproduce CI will not get Regal linting locally.
findings.evidence: scripts/scp-policy-check lines 358-365 read_tool_version opa and conftest only; no REGAL_VERSION assignment, no download_regal function, no regal lint invocation anywhere in the file. scripts/.tool-versions line 3 now carries 'regal 0.40.0' which the local script never consumes. contrast with policy-check.yml lines 175+203+241-253+422-445 which fully integrate Regal.
findings.impact: A Rego style regression caught by 'regal lint' in CI would not be surfaced by a local scp-policy-check run. The tool-versions Regal entry is functionally dead code in the local repro path. The CI supply-chain gate at policy-check.yml lines 422-445 is fully intact — this is a local-parity gap only.
findings.mitigation: Option A (preferred): add download_regal (bare binary, no archive — mirror download_opa structure) and a regal lint invocation to scripts/scp-policy-check, reading REGAL_VERSION via read_tool_version and SHA256 via json_lock_field. Option B (acceptable): add explicit --help text and a script-level comment stating Regal linting is CI-only and cannot be reproduced locally without a pre-installed regal binary in PATH.

findings.mitigation: Change 'TWO places' to 'THREE places' in DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 95.

findings.claim: The Regal smoke test at policy-check.yml line 296 suppresses both stdout and stderr: '"${BIN_DIR}/regal" version >/dev/null 2>&1'. If the binary fails its smoke test, only the emit_infra_failure string 'Regal runtime failed its post-download smoke test' appears in the runner log; regal's own error output (e.g. dynamic linker error, incompatible kernel version) is discarded, reducing fault diagnosis fidelity for the SHA-passing-but-corrupt-binary edge case.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml line 296: '"${BIN_DIR}/regal" version >/dev/null 2>&1 || emit_infra_failure "Regal runtime failed its post-download smoke test"'. Both stdout and stderr are null-routed. This edge case requires a binary that (a) passes sha256sum comparison and (b) fails at runtime — e.g. cross-architecture binary, glibc mismatch, or FS-level bit flip after download.
findings.impact: Diagnostic quality only; no correctness or security impact. SHA256 verification (primary hard-fail control) must already have passed before the smoke test runs.
findings.mitigation: Drop the 2>&1 redirect so regal's stderr flows to the runner log: '"${BIN_DIR}/regal" version >/dev/null || emit_infra_failure "Regal runtime failed its post-download smoke test"'.
